issues.description: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE constant duplicated across three locations — single source of truth violated
issues.detail: The string 'python:3.12' is declared in backend/kale/pipeline.py (DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE), re-declared as a TypeScript constant in labextension/src/widgets/cell-metadata/CellMetadataEditor.tsx, and hardcoded as a fallback literal in labextension/src/lib/Commands.ts getDefaultBaseImage. The entire purpose of introducing the constant is centralization; instead, three independent copies will silently drift when the default is bumped. Pick one authoritative source (the backend, served via RPC) and have any client-side fallback be a clearly-labeled degraded state, or fail loudly rather than hardcoding the literal again.

issues.description: _set_base_image silently changes semantics: empty-string fallback replaced by hardcoded python:3.12, overriding KFP default
issues.detail: Previously, when pod introspection failed (NotInClusterError, ApiException, missing pod), self.base_image was set to '' with a comment explicitly stating 'Use kfp default image', allowing downstream KFP to pick its own default. The diff now assigns DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE='python:3.12' eagerly, collapsing the tri-state distinction between 'unset / determined / fallback' into a single concrete value. This is a behavior change buried inside what was advertised as a UI feature, with no stated invariant and no regression test. Either revert this change, ship it as its own patch with justification, or document and test the new invariant explicitly.

issues.description: Effective-base-image resolution chain reimplemented at three different sites with overlapping defaulting layers
issues.detail: The precedence step.config.base_image -> pipeline base_image -> default is recomputed in the Jinja template, in InlineMetadata.createBaseImageText (baseImage || pipelineBaseImage || defaultBaseImage || DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE), and in the dialog placeholder in CellMetadataEditor. After the _set_base_image change, the template's third rung is unreachable because pipeline.base_image is now invariantly non-empty. Extract one pure resolver function returning {image, source} and call it from every site; remove the redundant defaulting layers so the contract lives in exactly one place.

issues.description: isDefault label in createBaseImageText is wrong when pipelineBaseImage is set
issues.detail: isDefault is computed as !this.props.baseImage, but effectiveImage may resolve to pipelineBaseImage — which is a pipeline-level override, not the system default. The UI will incorrectly display 'Base Image: <pipeline image> (default)' for steps inheriting the pipeline's image. Either compute the source explicitly (step / pipeline / default) and label accordingly, or only show '(default)' when neither step nor pipeline image is set.

issues.description: createBaseImageText now always renders, changing the visual contract for every existing step cell
issues.detail:
Previously the method returned '' (no element) when this.props.baseImage was falsy. It now unconditionally renders a

with the effective image and '(default)' suffix. Every step cell that previously had no Base Image line will now show one. If intentional, document the new contract; if not, gate the render on whether the cell actually has an explicit image or pass structured data ({image, source}) and render accordingly.

issues.description: Inline Input replaced by Button + modal Dialog — workflow regression for the common edit case
issues.detail: The previous UI exposed Base Image as an inline 25%-width Input field, editable in one interaction. The new UI hides editing behind a small 'IMAGE' button that opens a modal Dialog. The stated goal — surfacing the default — could have been achieved by setting the existing Input's placeholder to the resolved default, with zero added clicks and no Dialog machinery. The dialog adds framework cost without measured user benefit; reconsider whether the modal earns its complexity.

issues.description: New IMAGE button disabled when stepName is empty — precondition tightened versus old Input control with no user feedback
issues.detail: The new button has disabled={!(this.props.stepName && this.props.stepName.length > 0)}. The previous Input had no such gating; users could set the base image at any time. There is no tooltip or helper text explaining the constraint, and updateBaseImage already tolerates an empty stepName via `this.props.stepName || ''`. Either drop the precondition or surface why it exists.

issues.description: Button styled with width: '5%' on a contained MUI Button containing the text 'IMAGE'
issues.detail: A 5% width on a text-bearing button inside a parent of percentage width will clip, overflow, or render unpredictably depending on container. The wrapping div with padding:0 / marginRight:4px is similarly hand-tuned. This is a magic number disconnected from intent. Use content-sized width or a meaningful named size and align with surrounding layout conventions.

issues.description: getDefaultBaseImage swallows RPC errors and substitutes a hardcoded literal
issues.detail: On RPC failure the function returns 'python:3.12' — the very value the RPC was supposed to be the source of truth for. If the backend default ever changes and the RPC fails, the UI silently lies. Either propagate the error (render an 'unknown' / degraded state) or accept that the literal is part of a documented dual-language contract. As written, the code pretends to fetch truth while pre-deciding the answer.

issues.description: No tests added for the new default-resolution behavior, RPC, or pipeline.py semantic change
issues.detail: A new constant, a new template variable, a new RPC, a new fallback semantics in _set_base_image, and a four-level frontend resolution chain all ship with no tests in the diff. At minimum: a compiler-template test that default_base_image is rendered when neither step nor pipeline image is set; a regression test pinning the new _set_base_image postcondition; and a test that the resolution order yields the expected effective image and source label. The silent semantic shift in pipeline.py is exactly the kind of change that needs a regression test.

issues.description: Local 'from kale.pipeline import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE' inside get_default_base_image RPC
issues.detail: The import is placed inside the function body with no comment explaining why. There is no apparent circular import to break — kale.pipeline is a normal dependency for this module. Hoist the import to module scope, or if it is deferred deliberately, state the reason in a comment.

issues.description: Dedicated RPC for a static constant — round-trip without payoff given the client-side fallback
issues.detail: get_default_base_image exists solely to ship one string across the wire, but the frontend hardcodes the same literal as a silent fallback so the RPC never truly establishes single-source-of-truth. Either fold the value into an existing config/init payload, or commit to the RPC being authoritative and drop the client literal entirely.

issues.description: Reordering createBaseImageText and createLimitsText in InlineMetadata render with no stated rationale
issues.detail: The render block now emits createLimitsText() before createBaseImageText() where Base Image previously came first. This is an unrelated visible UI reordering buried in a feature PR. If intentional, state why; otherwise revert to keep the diff focused.

issues.description: Width arithmetic in the metadata row changed (35%->30%, +5% button) with no holistic layout pass
issues.detail: stepDependencies select width went from 35% to 30% and a 5%-wide button was added while the 25% base-image Input was removed. The row's total layout was nudged rather than redesigned; what fills the remaining space is implicit. Either own the row layout coherently (flex/grid) or leave the percentages alone.

issues.description: Reset to Default writes '' relying on truthy-coalesce semantics downstream
issues.detail: 'Reset to Default' calls updateBaseImage('') and relies on every downstream consumer treating '' as 'use default'. This is fragile: if any consumer ever stores '' deliberately, or validation rejects empty strings, the behavior breaks silently. Prefer an explicit null/undefined sentinel and a single helper that resolves the effective image.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges firmly on NEEDS-WORK. Two P0 defects dominate: the DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE constant is duplicated across pipeline.py, CellMetadataEditor.tsx, and a hardcoded fallback in Commands.ts — defeating the single-source-of-truth goal that motivated the PR — and _set_base_image silently changes semantics from '' (defer to KFP default) to a hardcoded python:3.12, a behavior change buried inside a UI feature with no test or stated invariant. Layered on top: the step/pipeline/default resolution chain is reimplemented at three sites with overlapping defaulting (template + InlineMetadata + dialog placeholder), the '(default)' label is mislabelled whenever pipelineBaseImage is set, and createBaseImageText now unconditionally renders, adding a line to every step cell that previously had none. The UX trade — replacing an inline Input with a Button + modal Dialog (plus an unexplained stepName precondition, a 5%-width 'IMAGE' button, and a swallowed-error RPC fallback) — buys nothing a placeholder on the existing Input couldn't deliver. Recommended path: split the patch, revert or justify the pipeline.py semantic change with a test, centralize the default in one authoritative place via one resolver function, and prefer placeholder text over the modal Dialog.
